correctness.rationale: Setting every chain coefficient to zero forces both loop endpoint values to vanish. The positive loop solution is therefore a Dirichlet mode with \(k=n\pi\). Substitution into the remaining quasi-\(\delta\) derivative equation gives exactly \(e^{i(\alpha_2-\alpha_1)}=(-1)^n\). The converse is the explicit sine mode, which is compactly supported and therefore square integrable. Disjoint loop supports give infinite multiplicity. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The relative loop phase is a principal symmetry-compatible parameter of the model. The theorem identifies its exact spectral role as a parity switch for strictly localized loop modes, including a complete absence statement for one-loop localization away from the two classes \(e^{i\alpha}=\pm1\) and an infinite-multiplicity consequence.
